item.title: Basin-Scale Nonlinear Dynamics of Thermohaline Ocean Circulation. Part I: Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.33383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Earth's thermohaline ocean circulation may support multiple equilibria and abrupt transitions. Similar bifurcation structures for different ocean models suggest common underlying dynamics across the model hierarchy. Here we propose a unifying framework from tracer conservation, in which surface fluxes are balanced by dissipative and advective tracer transport. We express this flux balance through a large-scale tracer gradient and a transport efficiency that measures how strongly circulation displaces the tracer field from its no-flow "conductive" state. The flux balance quantifies the transport contributions that sustain each circulation state and give rise to abrupt transitions. In a three-dimensional ocean-basin model, we find nonlinear salinity advection dominates the collapse threshold and linear dissipation dominates the recovery threshold. Temperature has additional dissipation from surface restoring, making thermal fluxes more dissipation-dominated than salinity fluxes. The tracer contrasts and boundary layers that a given circulation generates produce distinct transport regimes, approximately quadratic in circulation strength for weak flow and linear for strong flow. With a simple circulation closure, the flux balance reduces to longstanding box-model bifurcation results for the weak and strong flow regimes. Thus, by expressing thermohaline bifurcations through basin-scale transport, this framework connects box-model insight to the continuous equations. Furthermore, as this framework exposes the transport processes that balance a changing forcing, it provides constraints on a thermohaline ocean state and its trend toward tipping that overturning strength alone does not. In Part II, we develop flux-balance closures to forecast such tipping points.
item.dc:creator: Conner W. Lester, Dylan E. McNamara, Till J. W. Wagner

item.title: APEX: Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration
item.description: arXiv:2611.33450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensemble-based methods provide a practical framework for history matching, prediction, and optimization of subsurface models. In methodological studies, however, performance is rarely assessed from a single run. Comparisons typically span cases, configurations, and random seeds, while each evaluation may require an expensive external simulator. Keeping such studies computationally bounded, auditable, and reproducible therefore requires more than implementing a numerical method: experiments must be validated before execution, computational costs estimated, repeated runs organized consistently, and configurations and outputs made traceable. To address these needs, we developed APEX (Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration), an open-source Python platform that provides a common framework for configuring, validating, executing, recording, and comparing ensemble-based experiments. APEX is organized around three concepts: an experiment defines what is executed, a run records a single execution, and a study coordinates and compares multiple experiments or runs. Experiments are specified through validated configurations, which can also be generated by a planner agent. Before execution, APEX estimates the maximum number of forward simulations required. If the estimate exceeds a user-defined threshold, submission is held for approval. Each run records provenance information, while studies repeat problems across variants and paired replicates and compare results using paired statistical analyses. Scientific and computational components, including methods, simulators, metrics, and optimizers, are implemented as plugins. A command line interface, Python client, REST service with a web interface, and tools for language model agents access these capabilities through a common service layer.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Luo

item.title: Ion and electron temperature recovery for Irkutsk incoherent scatter measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.33902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovering ion and electron plasma temperatures from Irkutsk Incoherent Scatter Radar (IISR) data is a challenge due to rapid Faraday rotation, which significantly distorts signal correlation profiles. This paper presents an adaptation of the full-profile analysis (FPA) method tailored to the specific conditions of the IISR using a two-step inverse problem framework. The core novelty of the approach lies in the integration of data from both narrowband and wideband channels: experimental power profiles from the wideband channel are incorporated directly into the forward model for temperature recovery. By mathematically establishing the link between the wideband signal amplitude and the temperature ratio, we introduce a non-linear constraint that significantly narrows the solution search space. This addresses the problem of "stretched" global minima in the objective functional, effectively filtering out physically inconsistent results. The inverse problem is solved using the Improved Stochastic Ranking Evolution Strategy (ISRES), which enables fully automated parameter estimation without the need for manual initial guesses.
item.dc:creator: V. P. Tashlykov, A. V. Medvedev, V. P. Lebedev, I. V. Kichigin

item.title: Weak buoyancy and cold lithospheres decouple interior melting from seafloor volcanism on icy ocean worlds
item.description: arXiv:2611.33478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On icy ocean worlds, deep silicate melting can generate sufficient pressure to open fractures while magma freezes before reaching the ocean. We identify a coupled transport regime by linking finite melt segregation and nonlinear rock relaxation to fracture flow, crystallisation and the ice-loaded ocean boundary. In a hot Europa endmember, increasing grain size from 1 to 10 mm raises relaxed excess pressure from 5.55 kPa to 10.2 MPa, overcoming the inherited-fracture opening threshold despite weak buoyancy. For the same 100 m strike and 0.5 m aperture, the cold first-fill rate required by heat balance increases from 0.17-0.69 m3 s -1 over terrestrial crustal distances of 1.1-4.5 km to 15-29 m3 s -1 across 89-171 km Europa paths, far above the self-supplied flow. Higher ice-ocean pressure further reduces the enthalpy margin of near-solidus magma in the adopted basalt phase law. During approximately 5 kyr of dormancy, the collector pressure returns to its relaxed value, while upper-path walls cool to 275-282 K and the magma path loses liquid connectivity. In two focused Europa histories with mechanically supported pathways, delivery of 0.005 km3 of magma over 0.1 Myr requires 14-27 km3 of sacrificed magma-equivalent preparation material. Weak gravity, extensive cold rock and a pressurised ocean thus make seafloor access a history-dependent process governed by thermal connectivity and its renewal, decoupling recurrent volcanism from melt production at depth.
item.dc:creator: Nahiz Hestaphin

item.title: The linear Boltzmann equation in column experiments of porous media
item.description: arXiv:1908.00726v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The use of the linear Boltzmann equation is proposed for transport in porous media in a column. By column experiments, we show that the breakthrough curve is reproduced by the linear Boltzmann equation. The advection-diffusion equation is derived from the linear Boltzmann equation in the asymptotic limit of large propagation distance and long time.
item.dc:creator: Kenji Amagai, Motoko Yamakawa, Manabu Machida, Yuko Hatano
